column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3d background: company forecasts in Taiwan are voluntary by law (Art. 5), the basis of row 20's collapse and row 39's correction of claim 4; a reader's habit, never Taiwan law applied to Laura (out of the case's scope).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan allows a range only in the summary form; the split is about audit cost and detail, not certainty, so it says little about Laura's range.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d, the strongest Taiwan contrast: every company forecast must say it may not be completely achieved, and Laura's ends after the move need no such line; a reader's habit, never a legal question for Laura; the pencil-label turn in team prose only, never in Laura's words.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e at most, a correction to claim 1 (Taiwan's 20% is an update trigger with size floors, not an error margin); fix the use: after the move Laura's ends rest on no market assumption, but the 0.5% cut for the funds' other costs is still one (NUMBERS 4).

Mon 16 Nov: store or 3e: update versus correction is a clean split, but the mapping is incomplete: the missed deposit is behind her by March 2028, and the funds' other costs above the 0.5% cut can also lower an end (NUMBERS 4); say the IPS's two reasons are reasons to change the plan, not updates to a stated figure.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan's 2-day and 10-day notice clock; no notice duty applies to Laura, and a co-sponsor notice rule would be a new rule beside Table 3's seven rows.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c context: Taiwan grades forecasts in public each quarter; Laura's ends are graded once, in December 2032, and the contribution equals the stated top in every path tested (NUMBERS 4); weak parallel (earnings a firm controls against what bonds pay).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e: Taiwan's own list of a forecast's sensitive assumptions (exchange rates, interest rates, raw-material costs) maps onto 3e's areas 1 and 4: rates set the bottom and the top, the Taiwan dollar and building costs meet her flexibility (NUMBERS 8q); a reader's frame, never Taiwan law applied to Laura.

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q84-041 (Art. 19's one-month staleness beside the same NUMBERS 4 figures); its own disanalogy (stale data, not market paths) makes it the weaker; aha 7's wording fix applies to both.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, one clause at most: Taiwan makes a forecast carry its track record; Laura's nearest is the five ended iBond funds, all paid within 0.066% of their last market price (NUMBERS 0); five funds is a short record and IBTA ended 15 days early, so never ended on schedule.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d: TWSE treats a revenue range told to outsiders as a forecast that must be backed and kept current; Laura's range told to co-sponsors is backed by Treasuries held for her; listed firms only, so a parallel of principle; cut to one clause.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: TWSE's example range is 23.3% of its midpoint against Laura's 19.0% (Keel arithmetic); an example in a rule is not a norm, and Q35-029 and Q52 already give the width's yardsticks.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 context, store only: TWSE makes firms watch a forecast at all times and withdraw it at once; Laura watches the funds' notices, not her figure, which Table 3 row 4 already does.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan's forecast fines are modest (NT$240,000 to NT$4.8 million); context for row 15, and no part needs the amounts.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d: Taiwan priced a missed forecast as lost access to new money, not mainly a fine, which is the case's own warning (lose the confidence or participation of co-sponsors); a parallel in kind, since capital markets are not co-sponsors.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3c: Taiwan bars forecasts while an issuer raises money, and Laura states her figure as she asks; fix: the rule binds securities issuers, not Laura, so say the principle (a figure stated while asking for money should not be a forecast, and hers is not), never can only because; read the offering rules at source before citing (S 4).

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q35-028 (a width the speaker chooses invites suspicion; Laura's is set by a rule); Q35-032 already judged a stand-alone not-chosen line a slogan flip; if used, never each rounded down (SKELETON 3c, H2).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: MOPS names firms off forecast each quarter, so a miss costs reputation; supports row 15; the lists themselves were not read (S 4).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan's compulsory band (1991-2004) was dropped to stop over-optimistic forecasts; history behind rows 20-24, no part needs it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d guard and context: once free to choose, Taiwan's listed firms stopped forecasting (59.47% in 2003 to 0.58% in 2009), so the report never says co-sponsors are used to forecasts corrected by law; fix: date it (by 2009), since the 2026 TWSE count was not opened.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d tone: Taiwan's business readers get monthly actual revenue, not projections, so Laura's words should read as a reported fact with proof on request (SKELETON 3d checklist); a past figure against a future payment held, a parallel of tone only.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: under the hard band most forecasts were pulled back inside it; fix: 58.5% (Keel arithmetic) is measured against the authors' model of earnings before management, never against reported results, so say so every time.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a hard band brought earnings management, not accuracy; Laura's ends need nothing managed; abstracts only (S 4).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan IPO forecasts ran 11.4% above actual and a miss below 80% met only vague screening; supports row 15; conference paper, authors not captured.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan's volunteers chose the summary form; small, self-selected sample, no part needs it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: good news is told sooner; after the move Laura has no news to time, a thin use.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Japan's 10% / 30% revision test verified at source (claim 2 kept); context for rows 28-30, not a point for Laura.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: JPX judges each end of a range alone, so a range gives no shelter; after the move each of Laura's ends is held for her (NUMBERS 4); adds a regulator to Q71's listeners; the 99 / 110 example stays in the store.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: in Japan a moved forecast is a material fact under insider law; nobody trades on Laura's figure, so the use is thin.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: Japan's exchange had to tell investors a forecast is not a commitment and its revision is naturally expected; after the move Laura's figure can be heard as one; certain goes on the Treasuries, never on the amount (Q71-002).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: TSE asks firms to label the kind of figure (objective forecast, target, conservative commitment), which supports naming the sense the range answers (Q74-036): before the move the top is a forecast, after it money held; Japan's terms in team prose only, never in Laura's words.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: over 99% of Japanese forecasts are single figures; co-sponsors are in Taiwan and the case asks for a range, so it decides nothing.

Mon 16 Nov: store or 3c context: forecasters go quiet when uncertainty spikes (2020; US tariffs in 2025); fix: say what about 40% in 2020 counts (firms giving or withholding a forecast) and from which source; before the move her top is as exposed as any forecast.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c base rate, beside row 36 if one is needed: about 70% of Japanese firm-years revise (Nagata and Nguyen 2017, the citable source); Kato et al. only as cited; the Iwatani example stays in the store.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c base rate from a second sample (70.6%, Keel arithmetic) agreeing with row 34; author not captured, so cite row 34 if one figure is used.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, with row 30: the first forecast exactly right 74 times in 32,814; fix the contrast: the contribution equals the top because the top is set under what owned Treasuries pay and then capped, so it shows kind, never skill, and 0.2% is never set against every path as a score; the 95% is JPX 2025 (row 33), another span.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: last-minute revisions to the exact result show how forecasts are made right; old sample, thin use.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Japan fines false or hidden figures, not missed forecasts; neither 2026 case was a forecast, so no part needs it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d guard: claim 4's premise is false; give the figure, say in plain words what pays it, add no forecast label; Taiwanese foundations' and arts groups' own habits were not studied; Keel synthesis of rows 3, 11, 20, 21 (S 3).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3e: the short list of what can still move an end restates SKELETON 3d and Q76-038; fix: a missed deposit cannot move an end after March 2028, so list a Treasury default (said once in 3e as the IPS says it) and the funds' other costs above the 0.5% cut (about $119 per 0.1% centrally, NUMBERS 0), with no nothing-else slogan.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the top before the move as a forecast in Taiwan's sense, on NUMBERS 4's current figures (2.9%, 6.2%, 8.7%, 10.7%; gaps $1,745 to $5,263); fix per aha 7: a top named early would turn out larger than the move could buy, never not yet held; say simulated futures, not house paths (WORDS).

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q10e-019 (the same register sizes, NUMBERS 8q: $32,191 against $29,823, $2,368 short); the Art. 15 frame lives in Q84-008; certain in US dollars, not Taiwan dollars, is the useful 3e clause; never VT as a Taiwan-dollar hedge.
